form_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me choose a Delaware C-Corp formation service. Please research and compare Clerky, Stripe Atlas, and Firstbase, plus (if easily found) a traditional startup law firm alternative, so I can make an informed decision.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already known: my target incorporation timeline, whether I have co-founders and how many, expected initial funding source (bootstrapped, angel, accelerator, VC), whether I anticipate a Y Combinator or similar accelerator affiliation (some offer discounts), and my rough budget for formation costs.

Then research each candidate service and compile a comparison covering: pricing (base incorporation fee, ongoing annual fees like registered agent or compliance costs), what's included (bylaws, stock purchase agreements, 83(b) election help, board resolutions, cap table setup, EIN application), typical turnaround time, ease of use/reputation based on public reviews or founder discussions, and any notable limitations (e.g., lack of legal advice, rigid templates, add-on costs for amendments).

Organize your findings into a clear side-by-side table or structured summary, and add a short recommendation section explaining which option seems best suited to my stated situation and why, along with key trade-offs I should weigh (cost vs. flexibility vs. support level).

Do not create an account, submit any formation paperwork, or make payment on any platform. Your job is to prepare the comparison and a recommendation only.

When done, report back with the comparison table, your recommendation, and a short list of open questions or decisions only I can make (e.g., final structure preferences, share allocation). Then stop for human sign-off so I can review and choose the service myself.

form_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me check whether my desired company name is available for incorporation as a Delaware C-Corporation, before I proceed with filing.

If I haven't already given you the following, ask me for them:
- My preferred company name (e.g., "Acme Inc.")
- 2-3 backup name options in case the primary is unavailable
- Any required suffix I want to use (e.g., "Inc.", "Corporation", "Corp.")

Once you have these, please:
1. Go to the Delaware Division of Corporations' entity name search tool (the General Corporation Name Search on the state's ICIS system) and search for my primary desired name.
2. Record whether the name appears available or is already in use/reserved, noting any exact or confusingly similar matches shown in the results.
3. Repeat the search for each backup name I gave you, in order, and stop once you find one that appears available (or check all of them if I asked you to).
4. For each name checked, note the exact search term used and the result returned.
5. Summarize findings in a simple table: Name | Availability Status | Notes (e.g., similar existing entities found).

Done looks like: you have checked my primary name and all backups against the Delaware name database, and you can tell me clearly which name(s) appear available for use.

Important: this search only checks current availability and does not reserve the name or guarantee final acceptance by the state — actually reserving or filing with a chosen name remains a human step, since it may require submitting forms, paying fees, or making decisions I should confirm myself. Do not attempt to reserve or file anything on my behalf.

Report back to me with the availability results table, which name(s) you recommend based on availability, and any next steps I should take to reserve or file with my chosen name.

form_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare (but NOT submit) the Delaware C-Corp incorporation filing using {{vendor}}, a legal-ops incorporation platform. Do not attest to, sign, or file anything on my behalf — Delaware law requires an authorized human incorporator/officer to do that.

First, ask me for any missing inputs: company name (plus 2-3 backup names), registered agent details, number of authorized shares and par value, founder/officer names and addresses, stock split among founders, and whether a stock purchase agreement and vesting schedule are needed.

Then use {{vendor}}'s guided questionnaire or, if available, its document-set API (using my configured credentials) to populate the Certificate of Incorporation, bylaws, initial board resolutions, and stock purchase agreements based on my answers. Flag any questions or choices the tool marks as needing attorney review, and list them clearly for me.

Once the document set is generated, compile a summary showing: company name and share structure, registered agent, list of documents drafted, any attorney-review flags, and the current status/link within {{vendor}} where I (or the authorized officer) can review and sign. Note that the Delaware Division of Corporations filing itself (https://corp.delaware.gov/howtoform/) also requires human submission and attestation.

Do not click submit, sign, attest, or authorize the filing in {{vendor}} or on the Delaware portal — this remains a human step. Prepare everything up to the point of signature/filing, then stop for human sign-off and report back with the summary above so I can review and authorize the actual submission myself.

form_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me track the receipt of my Delaware Certificate of Incorporation after filing to incorporate my C-Corp. Delaware's Division of Corporations (or my registered agent, if I used one to file) is processing the filing on its own internal timeline, and actually issuing the stamped certificate remains a human step — Delaware's state processing queue controls when it arrives, and there is no system for you to operate to speed this up.

First, ask me for: (1) the filing date I submitted the Certificate of Incorporation, (2) whether I filed directly with Delaware's Division of Corporations or through a registered agent/formation service, and (3) any confirmation number or reference ID I received at filing time.

Once I provide that, please prepare a monitoring checklist for me:
- The expected turnaround window based on whether I chose standard or expedited processing (note that I should confirm the specific timeframe with Delaware's Division of Corporations or my registered agent, since processing times vary).
- Instructions for how I can check status: via the Delaware Division of Corporations' online status lookup (if I have a file number) or by contacting my registered agent's support channel.
- A reminder of what the finished deliverable looks like: a stamped/certified Certificate of Incorporation PDF or paper copy showing the state's approval date and file number.
- A note that once received, the certificate should be saved to my company's official records/document storage as the foundational legal document, since later steps (bylaws, stock purchase agreements, board resolutions) depend on it.

Do not attempt to file, resubmit, or contact Delaware on my behalf — just prepare the checklist and status-check instructions. Report back with the checklist, the expected timeframe, and clear next steps for me to verify receipt myself, noting explicitly that waiting for Delaware to issue the certificate remains a human step outside your control.

form_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare bylaws and initial board resolutions for our new Delaware C-Corporation using {{vendor}}, a legal-ops platform. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any missing inputs needed to complete the intake questionnaire: company legal name, incorporation state (Delaware), total authorized shares and par value, founder/officer/director names and titles, initial stock split among founders, vesting terms if any, indemnification provisions, and registered agent details.
2. Log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials and open (or start) the incorporation workflow for this company.
3. Complete the guided questionnaire fields with the inputs I provide, using {{vendor}}'s standard templates for bylaws and initial board consents/resolutions rather than drafting from scratch.
4. Flag any questionnaire choices that {{vendor}} marks as needing attorney review (e.g., non-standard equity splits, custom indemnification language, unusual vesting) and list them separately in your report.
5. Generate draft bylaws and initial board resolutions within {{vendor}}, but do not submit, finalize, e-sign, or approve any documents.
6. Prepare a summary checklist showing: what inputs were used, which documents were drafted, which items were auto-flagged for legal review, and what remains outstanding.

Done looks like: draft bylaws and initial resolutions exist in {{vendor}} in an unsubmitted/draft state, all flagged review items are clearly listed, and nothing has been signed or approved.

Report back with: the current status in {{vendor}}, a link or reference to the draft documents, the list of flagged items needing attorney/founder review, and any inputs still needed from me. Then stop for human sign-off — do not sign, approve, or submit any documents on my behalf.

form_001:n6b.prompt:
You are helping me prepare (but not execute) the signature packet for my Delaware C-Corp's bylaws and initial board consent. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any missing inputs: the corporation's exact legal name, Delaware file number (if issued), incorporation date, registered agent name, names/titles of the incorporator and initial director(s)/officer(s), and where the draft bylaws and board consent documents currently live (e.g., a shared drive link or file I'll provide).

2. Locate or organize the draft bylaws and initial board consent documents, checking that each includes correct corporate name, date, and signature blocks with proper titles (e.g., Incorporator, Director, Secretary).

3. Prepare a signature-ready packet: consolidate the documents in order (bylaws first, then board consent), verify all blanks (dates, names, share counts, registered agent info) are filled in consistently across documents, and flag any inconsistencies or missing information for me to resolve.

4. If I want to use an e-signature tool, help me set up the envelope/request using my configured credentials (adding signer names, emails, and signature fields) but do not send it or mark any fields as signed.

5. Produce a short checklist confirming: documents are complete, signer names/titles match corporate records, and the packet is ready for signature.

Do not sign, initial, approve, or submit these documents on my behalf under any circumstance — executing the bylaws and board consent is a legal act of corporate authority that only I or another authorized officer/director can perform. Once the packet is fully prepared and checked, stop for human sign-off and report back with a summary of what's ready, any open issues needing my input, and the location of the finalized packet.

form_001:n7.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the founder stock issuance paperwork for our new Delaware C-Corp using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops platform. This step only prepares documents for my review and board approval — do not submit, sign, or finalize anything.

First, ask me for any missing inputs you need:
- {{vendor}} account login status (confirm I have access; use my configured credentials, do not ask me to share them)
- Company legal name and state of incorporation (Delaware)
- List of founders, their full legal names, and email addresses
- Total authorized shares and each founder's intended share allocation (number of shares or percentage)
- Price per share (or par value) for the stock purchase
- Vesting schedule details (e.g., standard 4-year vesting with 1-year cliff, or custom terms)
- Any founders receiving accelerated vesting or special terms

Then, in {{vendor}}:
1. Log in and navigate to the founder stock issuance / post-incorporation setup workflow.
2. Complete the guided questionnaire using the inputs above, entering each founder's allocation, price per share, and vesting terms.
3. Let the platform generate the stock purchase agreements, board resolution language, and 83(b) election paperwork for each founder.
4. Flag any questionnaire prompts the platform marks as needing attorney review, and list them separately in your report.
5. Do not approve, sign, or submit the documents on my behalf — leave them in draft/pending status.

When done, report back with: a summary of the share allocations and terms entered, links or references to the drafted documents in {{vendor}}, and a bullet list of any flagged items requiring attorney or board attention. Then stop for human sign-off before any approval or filing occurs.

form_001:n7b.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the founder stock purchase agreements for our new Delaware C-Corporation so they are ready for founders to sign. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any missing details: legal company name, state of incorporation (Delaware), each founder's full legal name and email address, total shares being purchased by each founder, price per share/par value, vesting schedule terms (if any, e.g., 4-year vesting with 1-year cliff), and whether final agreement drafts already exist (from our formation attorney or incorporation service) or need to be assembled from a template.

2. If drafts don't exist yet, compile the stock purchase agreement for each founder using the standard terms I provide, filling in founder name, share count, purchase price, vesting terms, and effective date. Keep the agreements consistent across founders except for individual-specific fields.

3. Prepare each agreement for electronic signature using a standard e-signature service such as DocuSign or Adobe Sign (using my configured credentials for that service): upload the document, add each founder as a signer with the correct signature and date fields, and set up the signing order if applicable.

4. Do not send the agreements for signature or trigger any signature request yet, and do not sign, approve, or submit on my behalf.

5. Prepare a checklist summarizing: each founder's document, share/price/vesting terms, signer emails, and the e-signature workflow status, so I can review everything before it goes out.

When done, report back: the drafted or compiled agreement contents (or confirmation they match the attorney-provided version), the e-signature envelope/draft ready for review, and the checklist. Because the founders must personally execute a binding contractual obligation to purchase shares, this remains a human step — stop for human sign-off before any agreement is sent or signed.

form_001:n8a.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the 83(b) election filing for my Delaware C-Corp founder stock purchase. This is a time-sensitive IRS election that must be personally signed and postmarked within 30 days of my stock purchase/grant date, so accuracy and speed of preparation matter.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for any missing details: my full legal name, home address, Social Security Number (do not store or transmit this beyond drafting the document text — I will fill it in myself if you prefer not to handle it), the corporation's legal name, EIN (if issued), Delaware incorporation date, number of shares purchased, purchase price per share, fair market value per share at grant, grant/purchase date, and vesting schedule terms from the stock purchase agreement.
2. Draft the standard 83(b) election letter using this information, formatted per IRS requirements (statement of election, taxpayer info, description of property, dates, values, and consideration paid).
3. Prepare a cover letter to the IRS service center appropriate for my state of residence, and a checklist of required copies (one for IRS filing, one for my records, one for the corporation's records).
4. Prepare mailing instructions noting that IRS guidance recommends certified mail with return receipt for proof of timely filing, and calculate and clearly flag the 30-day deadline date based on the grant date I provide.
5. Summarize everything in a clear checklist: what's drafted, what's missing, and the exact deadline date.

Do not sign, date, or submit anything on my behalf — I must personally sign the election and mail it myself, since IRS rules require the taxpayer's own certification and this is a personal tax filing you cannot execute for me. Once your draft package and checklist are ready, stop for human sign-off and report back what you prepared, what I still need to supply, and the deadline date.

form_001:n8.prompt:
You are helping me prepare an 83(b) election filing with the IRS for stock I (or a founder/employee) recently purchased in our new Delaware C-Corp. This election must be physically mailed to the IRS within 30 days of the stock purchase date, and there is no e-file option — signing and mailing remains a human step.

First, ask me for any missing details you need:
- Taxpayer's full name, address, and SSN/TIN
- Corporation's name, EIN (if issued), and address
- Date of stock purchase, number of shares, type of stock, purchase price, and fair market value at purchase
- Description of the restrictions on the stock (e.g., vesting schedule)
- The IRS service center address for our jurisdiction (look this up if needed)

Then do the following:
1. Download the official IRS Form 15620 from https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f15620.pdf.
2. Fill in the form fields using the details I provided, double-checking accuracy of dates, share counts, and valuations.
3. Prepare a cover letter or checklist noting: (a) the form must be printed and signed with an original wet signature, (b) copies should be made for my records, one for the corporation, and one for my tax return, (c) it must be mailed via certified mail with return receipt requested to the correct IRS address, and (d) the postmark date must be within 30 days of the purchase date.
4. Calculate and clearly flag the exact deadline date (purchase date + 30 days) so I don't miss it.
5. Draft a simple tracking note for me to log the certified mail tracking number once sent, so I can verify IRS receipt later.

Once you've prepared the completed draft form, cover letter, mailing instructions, and deadline calculation, present them to me and stop for human sign-off — I will personally sign and physically mail the form, since signing and mailing remains a human step you cannot perform. Report back with the completed draft, the calculated deadline, and the mailing checklist.
